upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. His name is Alex and he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any of that. He finished school and decided not to continue with A-levels or anything like that. He's working now instead.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me explain why:

Child Benefit can generally be claimed for children who are:
- Under 16, **or**
- 16, 17, 18, 19 or 20 and in approved education or training

Since Alex is 17 and is no longer in approved education or training (he's working instead), he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Before I confirm this, may I just ask one more question: Is Alex registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation as someone who is not in education, employment or training (NEET)? In some cases, there can be a short extension period after leaving education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not registered with anything like that. He went straight into work after leaving school, so he's been employed full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you a final assessment on your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:**
Alex is 17 years old and has left school to work full-time. He is not in approved education or training, and he is not registered with a careers service. 

Child Benefit can only be claimed for children aged 16 or over if they remain in **approved education or training** (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to Level 3, or traineeships). Since Alex doesn't meet these criteria, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he decides to return to approved education or training—you may be able to make a new claim at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
